intended_object: For a ring R, a finite index type n and an index p, this is the additive map R/[R,R] → M_n(R)/[M_n(R),M_n(R)] induced by r ↦ r·E_pp, which puts r in the (p,p) corner. It is the inverse of the trace isomorphism on quotients by additive commutators (Weibel, K-book II §2). Inferred from the docstring, the module doc and its use in `traceQuotientEquiv`.
explanation:
`Ring.additiveCommutators` is the additive subgroup generated by all ab − ba, which is the standard [R,R]. The definition applies `QuotientAddGroup.map` to `singleAddMonoidHom p p` (r ↦ single p p r). The proof `additiveCommutators_le_corner_comap` justifies this, using E_pp(ab) − E_pp(ba) = [aE_pp, bE_pp]. On classes it sends [r] to [single p p r], as the lemma `cornerOnCommutatorQuotient_mk` records. This is exactly the intended corner map.

The library uses it as the inverse of the trace map in `traceQuotientEquiv`, and proves that it does not depend on p.

Generality is right: the construction is stated for a ring R (the setting of Weibel and of the module) and an arbitrary finite index type. Finiteness is needed for the matrix ring structure. One could weaken to non-unital rings, but that is not the standard setting for this construction and not a meaningful narrowing.

Mathlib has no counterpart: I did not find a trace or corner map on additive-commutator quotients there.
